prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Can you please hand over (A) / any books on microeconomics (B) / that you can spare from your library? (C) / No Error (D)
options: that you can spare from your library? (C)
explanation: In interrogative sentences that express a request, 'some' replaces 'any', so it should be 'some books on microeconomics'.

along with him to the examination hall, (B)

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. We have not received some information from our coast guards yet.
explanation: In a negative sentence 'any' replaces 'some': 'have not received any information'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. I did not see anybody in the auditorium. /No error
explanation: 'Anybody' is correct in a negative sentence and the tense and preposition are appropriate, so there is no error.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. John searched thoroughly but could not find his coat nowhere in the house.
explanation: 'Could not' is already negative, so 'nowhere' creates a double negative; it must be 'anywhere in the house'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.
sentence: I do not see some reasons why my application should be rejected.
explanation: 'Any' is used in negative sentences instead of 'some', and 'reason why' is the correct collocation.

sentence: If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement’. He has hardly some near friends.
explanation: 'Hardly' is already negative in sense, so it pairs with 'any', and the correct collocation is 'close friends', not 'near friends'.
